story.title: This open-source project lets you sync Withings data to other apps without a subscription

facts.text: As Withings clarified, existing users are grandfathered in and retain free automatic sync to third-party services.
This exemption is tied to your Withings account rather than any physical device, so you can purchase new hardware without triggering the paywall.
However, such a move erodes customer confidence in the product ecosystem and casts doubt on the future.
As an owner of a Withings Body Smart scale myself, I’d think twice about a new Withings purchase despite the grandfathering.

Withings responded to a customer complaint thread, announcing that the company has officially moved automatic third-party app syncing behind its paid Withings Plus subscription tier for any accounts created on or after October 13, 2026.
While the initial outrage from customers was around Apple Health sync, the change also applies to Android users relying on Google Health Connect .
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission.
Withings isn’t the first smart health brand to try and monetize its ecosystem beyond the hardware.
However, in terms of monetization, other smart health brands monetize predictive analytics and AI-based coaching features rather than holding data hostage.
Without (free) automatic syncing back into the wider platform, I have a harder time recommending the smart scale to new users.
User sentiment in Withings’ support thread echoes my own, as expected.
Smart health hardware these days has increasingly leaned on recurring software subscriptions to further monetize the user base, but Withings’ latest move is now crossing a line.
The silver lining for new and future Withings users is that their data isn’t completely held hostage (yet).
All users can still manually export their historical health records as CSV or PDF without a subscription.
Newly registered users receive a standard trial period to test Withings Plus features.
Anthony’s solution was to create an open-source project called YourOwnWeigh that reroutes your data away from Withings’ servers so it can be wirelessly synced to other apps and platforms for free.

When it was revealed earlier this month that Withings would require new users to subscribe to a Withings Plus subscription to sync heath data from the company’s devices to third-party apps, Tom Anthony, who was already fed up with the Withings mobile app which they describe as a “bloated mess,” became motivated to “free” their scales.
The YourOwnWeigh web app handles several tasks, including using Bluetooth to update Withings scales with alternate firmware so they upload data to a non-Withings server you’ve configured.
YourOwnWeigh is also currently limited to just two older models of Withings’ scales.
Instead of hosting a copy of Withings’ firmware, it’s downloaded and patched as needed.
